summary.one_liner: procs is a Rust-written replacement for the Unix `ps` command that shows colored, human-readable process listings with extra fields such as ports, I/O throughput and Docker container names.
summary.what_it_does: It lists processes with colored, configurable columns and automatic light/dark theme detection. Users can search by keyword (non-numeric matches USER and Command by default; numeric matches PID) and combine multiple keywords with AND, OR, NAND or NOR logic. It adds fields ps lacks, including TCP/UDP ports, read/write throughput, Docker container names and more memory details. It also offers a watch mode that refreshes like top, a tree view of parent/child processes, sorting and column insertion options, and automatic pager use. Configuration is done through a TOML file, and shell completions can be generated for zsh, bash, fish, PowerShell and elvish.
use_cases: view and filter running processes in the terminal
replace ps with a more readable output
find which process is listening on a TCP or UDP port
watch processes update live like top
show processes as a parent/child tree
check Docker container names for running processes
notable: Column set is configurable via TOML, including per-column search and style settings
Value-aware coloring by percentage, process state and memory unit
Docker container name column via the Docker UNIX socket
Tree view and watch mode with keyboard sort controls
caveats: macOS support is experimental and only checked in GitHub Actions; FreeBSD is experimental too
Some information needs sudo or root, such as other users' process data, throughput and all listening ports on Linux
Docker Toolbox on macOS is not supported
